item.title: #3583005: Advertise truthful formats for unmarked datetimes and timestamps
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583005 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

Tool input schemas now describe what Drupal actually accepts. Timestamp inputs advertise integer seconds as well as RFC 3339 strings, so strict clients such as the MCP bridge, which validates arguments against the schema, no longer reject a bare integer. Datetime inputs with no date-only or date-time marker advertise both a full date-time and a bare date, instead of core's date-only date. Output schemas are not changed. If you have clients or tests that depend on the old advertised schema, expect the output of schema normalization to differ.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Advertised input JSON schema changes: core-path timestamp inputs become type: ["string","integer"] (plus null if optional); unmarked datetime_iso8601 inputs advertise anyOf of date-time and date formats.

Technical details

The change is in InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer (src/Normalizer/InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer.php). The issue text proposed advertising plain format: "date-time" for unmarked datetimes. The committed code differs: for an unmarked datetime_iso8601 input, it removes format and emits anyOf: [{format: date-time}, {format: date}], with the description note "An RFC 3339 date-time, or a date alone as YYYY-MM-DD." The comments in the code give the reason: the input coercion subscriber re-emits a full datetime in canonical form but leaves a bare Y-m-d date untouched, and naming only date-time would make a strict invoker reject the bare date. Marked definitions are unchanged: DateOnly gives date, DateTime gives date-time.

For timestamp on the core (11.1+) path, an input schema of type: string is widened to ["string", "integer"]. The note becomes "An RFC 3339 date-time or a Unix timestamp in seconds." This is skipped for OutputDefinitionInterface objects, because the output transform sends the string core describes. The legacy path already used integer and keeps its Unix-seconds note. The optional-input handling now also appends null to an array-valued type, so a union gains the null branch the same way a single string type does. Unmarked datetime outputs are deliberately left alone, since the output transform only rewrites to RFC 3339 under the DateTime marker. The commit also updates the schema matrix and acceptance tests.

item.title: #3583043: Output definitions cannot say "always present, may be null"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583043 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

Output definitions can now say a value is always sent but may be null, such as a photo's EXIF date or a timestamp that has not happened yet. Before, one required flag meant both "key must be present" and "never null", so such outputs were published as optional and possibly missing. This also changes existing behavior: an optional output that holds NULL is now left out of the result, and its published schema no longer advertises null. The change landed before rc1 because it alters the published schema of every optional output.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Custom classes implementing OutputDefinitionInterface must implement isNullable() and setNullable(). Optional outputs set to NULL are now omitted from the result, and their schema no longer includes null.
  • New API: nullable constructor parameter and isNullable() / setNullable() on output definitions (OutputDefinitionInterface, NullableOutputTrait), default FALSE.

Technical details

required now means key presence only. A new nullable flag, default FALSE, means null is a value the output carries. This is provided by NullableOutputTrait (isNullable() / setNullable()), added to OutputDefinitionInterface and to the OutputDefinition, ListOutputDefinition, MapOutputDefinition and EntityOutputDefinition constructors as a trailing bool $nullable = FALSE argument.

The four combinations behave as follows:

  • required: TRUE, nullable: FALSE: the key is always present and never null.
  • required: TRUE, nullable: TRUE: the key is always present, may be null, and is listed in the parent's required with [T, "null"] as its type.
  • required: FALSE, nullable: FALSE: an output holding NULL is left out of the result.
  • required: FALSE, nullable: TRUE: the output may be missing or null, and its type is [T, "null"].

InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer reads isNullable() for outputs and strips the null branch (removeNullBranch()) from non-nullable outputs. Inputs keep the old rule, where an optional input is nullable. EffectiveDataDefinition does not mark a nullable output required, so core's NotNull is not added.

Runtime handling is in several places. setOutputValue() and ToolBase drop an optional non-nullable output set to NULL. validateOutputs() uses array_key_exists() to tell "set to NULL" from "never set", so a required nullable output set to NULL passes. The same rule applies inside maps through RecursiveToolValueTransformSubscriber: a null in an optional, non-nullable property is removed. A null list item is not removed, because that would shift the positions after it. It fails validation unless the item definition is nullable. ListOutputDefinition::createFrom() carries the flag on the list itself and sets it FALSE on the item.

TypedMethodDescriber now maps nullable method-tool return types and members to required plus nullable. omit_when_null maps to optional and non-nullable. memberIsRequired() and its @todo were replaced by memberAllowsNull(). Input-side nullable is left to a follow-up issue.

Upgrade

For an output that is always sent and may hold null, declare both flags:

new OutputDefinition('timestamp', 'Date', 'When the photo was taken.', required: TRUE, nullable: TRUE);

Optional outputs that relied on sending an explicit null now need nullable: TRUE. Without it, a NULL value is dropped from the result and the schema no longer lists null.

item.title: #3630882: Store the OAuth2 client identifier on tokens
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 6.1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +213/−7 · php +213/−7
  • Diff: aa563c3
  • Discussion: #3630882 · 4 contributors · 9 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 4 contributors

Summary

OAuth2 tokens now record the client identifier (the same value the server uses in requests and in the access token aud claim) in a new client_id field. Before, a token only pointed to a saved consumer entity. This is groundwork for allowing clients that are not saved consumer entities (#3630879). Existing tokens are filled in by a database update, so run updates after deploying. The old client reference is kept.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: simple_oauth_update_8609() installs a new indexed client_id string field on oauth2_token and backfills it from each token's referenced consumer.
  • New API: New client_id base field on the oauth2_token entity type, holding the OAuth2 client identifier the token was issued to.

Technical details

Oauth2Token::baseFieldDefinitions() adds a non-translatable client_id string field (max length 255) and lists it in field_indexes. TokenEntityNormalizer sets it from $client->getIdentifier(). RefreshTokenEntityNormalizer sets it from $token_entity->getAccessToken()->getClient()->getIdentifier(). The client entity reference is still written by TokenEntityNormalizer.

simple_oauth_update_8609() installs the field storage definition. It then copies client_id from consumer_field_data (default language rows only) into oauth2_token, matching on the token's client column. Tokens with no consumer reference stay NULL.

ExpiredCollector::collectForClient() now matches on an OR group of client (consumer entity ID) and client_id ($client->getClientId()). This differs from the issue's proposal to query by client_id alone. The code comment says matching the reference as well finds tokens issued before a consumer's client ID changed. Kernel tests cover token creation across the authorization code flow and the update path. The unit test for the collector was adjusted for the OR group.

Upgrade

Run database updates (drush updb) to apply simple_oauth_update_8609(), which adds the client_id field to oauth2_token and backfills existing tokens from their consumers.

item.title: #3588999: Add drupal-ckeditor5-plugins skill: CKEditor 5 plugin customization, version alignment, and installation methods
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3588999 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The ai_best_practices project has a new skill, drupal-ckeditor5-plugins, for AI coding agents that customize CKEditor 5 in Drupal. It targets three recurring agent mistakes: reading the latest CKEditor docs instead of the version bundled in the site's core, shipping raw ES modules where Drupal 10.3 to 11 needs a webpack DLL bundle, and mixing the DLL method with the new-builds (UMD) method used from Drupal 12 and CKEditor 5 v48. It also tells agents to look for an existing plugin in core, the CKEditor 5 Plugin Pack or Premium Features before writing a custom one. The Drupal 12 guidance is flagged as beta.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New drupal-ckeditor5-plugins skill under skills/ with five reference files and an eval set under evals/drupal-ckeditor5-plugins/.

Technical details

SKILL.md makes the version check a required Step 0. The agent reads the version: under ckeditor5: in core/core.libraries.yml and uses it to pin all CKEditor docs lookups. It then routes to reference files through a task table. Detailed content sits in references/: version-matrix.md, custom-plugins-dll.md, drupal-12-outlook.md, plugin-pack-premium-features.md and agent-docs.md. This follows the progressive-disclosure pattern of the drupal-gitlab skill.

version-matrix.md deliberately gives a derivation procedure instead of a static table. The bundled CKEditor version can change between patch releases of one core minor, and it may carry a -drupal.A fork suffix. The docs URL is derived by truncating to <major>.<minor>.0, because exact-patch URLs return 404.

SKILL.md also lists cross-cutting rules. Check for existing plugins even when the user explicitly asks for a custom one. Bundling is mandatory on Drupal 10 and 11. The DLL and new-builds methods are mutually exclusive per Drupal major. The plugin key chain across <module>.ckeditor5.yml, the webpack library: ['CKEditor5', '<namespace>'] output and <module>.libraries.yml must match exactly. Plugin source must import only from ckeditor5/src/*.

The issue states that evals are added under evals/drupal-ckeditor5-plugins/, with static checks plus five behavioral cases. The directory contains static-checks.json, dataset.yaml, rubrics.yaml and README.md. The issue says a refresh of references/drupal-12-outlook.md is a follow-up once the 2.x Plugin Pack and Premium Features modules ship their 2.0.0-beta.

item.title: #3583065: Report item and property positions in the violation path, not the message
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583065 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Tool module, a validation failure on a list item or map property now reports where it happened in the violation's property path (code, codes.0, rows.0.sku). Before, the position was embedded in the message text, e.g. (item 0) .... Output validation failures now follow the same shape as input failures: the output name is on the path and the message states only the reason. The plain-text failure message still shows the path in front of each reason, so Drush-style text consumers still see where the failure is. Code that parsed (item N) or (property x) out of messages, or that matched the old output messages, needs updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Violation property paths for list items and map properties now carry the position (code, codes.0, rows.0.sku); the (item N) and (property x) message prefixes are gone. Output violations carry the output name on the path with generic messages, and getViolations() is now populated on output failures.

Technical details

ValueViolationsTrait::addItemViolations() no longer takes a $kind argument and no longer wraps the message. It rebuilds each violation with static::joinPath($position, $violation->getPropertyPath()), and now also passes the constraint through to the new violation. validateInputValues() now uses it for the input name too, replacing its own rebuild loop. TypedOutputsTrait::validateOutputs() uses it to put the output name on the path. getItemDefinitionForViolations() is removed, since messages no longer need the item's label, and callers use $definition->getItemDefinition().

Messages that named the value by label became generic and name-free, because the name is now on the path: This output is required but was not provided., This property is required., This output must be an entity., This output is invalid: @type.. The required-output violation now carries the output name as its path instead of an empty string.

ToolBase now builds the Runtime failure from ToolMessages::violationList($violations) and passes $violations to ExecutableResult::failure(). ToolResultInterface::getViolations() therefore covers output failures as well as input failures. Callers can use getFailureCategory() to tell an input they can correct from an output the tool got wrong. The ToolResultInterface docblock documents the path format: the name is the segment before the first dot, and a map property reads product.sku, a list item codes.0, both rows.0.sku.

Upgrade

Read the position from the violation path instead of the message. Messages like (item 0) This value should be of the correct primitive type. are now path codes.0 with the message This value should be of the correct primitive type.

foreach ($result->getViolations() as $violation) {
  $path = $violation->getPropertyPath(); // e.g. "rows.0.sku"; first segment is the input or output name.
}

  • Opened: September 25, 2026

item.title: #3583086: Let `destructive` be undeclared, so write tools aren't reported as non-destructive
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583086 · 1 contributor · 5 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

The Tool module can now tell a tool that never declared destructive apart from one that said it is not destructive. An undeclared Write or Trigger tool is now treated as destructive, and an undeclared Read tool is not. Before, every write tool that left the flag out looked non-destructive, so the MCP bridge told clients it only added data. That is the opposite of MCP's own default. Authors of write tools that only add data should now set destructive: FALSE explicitly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: destructive on #[Tool], #[ToolMethod] and ToolDefinition::setDestructive() is now ?bool defaulting to NULL (undeclared); ToolDefinition::isDestructive() answers from the operation when undeclared.

Technical details

destructive on the #[Tool] and #[ToolMethod] attributes and the ToolDefinition::$destructive property changed from bool defaulting to FALSE to ?bool defaulting to NULL. ToolDefinition::setDestructive() accepts ?bool. ToolDefinition::isDestructive() now returns $this->destructive ?? $this->getOperation()->isModifying(). ToolOperation::isModifying() is TRUE for Write and Trigger and FALSE for Explain, Read and Transform. An explicit TRUE or FALSE always wins over the operation. #[ToolMethod] defaults its operation to Write, so a method that omits destructive is now destructive.

The Drush ToolGenerator prompt now defaults its answer to what an undeclared tool would get for the chosen operation. tool.twig always writes destructive: TRUE or FALSE instead of omitting it when false, so answering no on a Write tool is an explicit declaration. The issue body says the MCP bridge (mcp_server_tool_bridge) sends this as destructiveHint. The commit does not touch that bridge, which gets the new value through isDestructive(). The issue was meant to land before the RC1 freeze (#3582976).

Upgrade

Write or Trigger tools that only add data and relied on the old default must now say so:

#[ToolMethod(id: 'tool_test.notebook.export', operation: ToolOperation::Write, permission: 'access content', destructive: FALSE)]

Code that passes destructive: FALSE or TRUE is unchanged. Code that reads isDestructive() still gets a bool.

item.title: #3583091: Name the input when an entity handle fails, so getViolations() covers handle failures
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583091 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

When a tool call is given a malformed, missing or wrong-type entity handle, the failed result now says which input was at fault. Before, getViolations() was empty for these failures and the message was only a generic "Invalid input" text. A caller, such as an AI agent, can now see every bad input in one response and fix them together.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

HandleExceptionInterface is a bare marker with no input context, so ToolRunner could only produce Invalid input: @message with no violations. The issue weighed two options: a per-input catch in the runner, or an InputAwareExceptionInterface with getInputNames(). The merged code takes the per-input catch. It adds no new interface.

In ToolRunner, the loop that calls $tool->setInputValue() now catches HandleExceptionInterface for each input. It records a ConstraintViolation whose property path is the input name, built by the new private handleViolation(). A HandleNotFoundException gets an extra sentence saying a handle resolves only for the account that created it, until it expires. A refiner that throws is attributed to the input whose set triggered it.

The loop also catches InputException per input. Its named violations join the same list. A bare-reason exception keeps its own message as the whole result unless another input has already failed. The runner collects every input that cannot be stored before refusing the call. It then runs validateInputs() on the inputs that were stored and adds those violations, skipping the inputs that failed to store, so a bad value shows up beside a bad handle. The combined list is set with setFailureResult() using FailureCategory::Input. The private inputNamed() reads the first segment of a violation path to do that filtering. The outer HandleExceptionInterface catch remains only for handle exceptions thrown after the input loop, such as an output transform, which have no input to name.

item.title: #3588983: Git ignore ai_best_practices.yaml file?
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3588983 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

The drupal/ai_best_practices Composer plugin now adds /ai_best_practices.yaml to the project's .gitignore when it first creates that file. The file holds per-developer settings, such as the skills output directory and excluded skills. The issue reporter had committed it and got deployment errors on Pantheon. The README now has a "What to commit" section. It says to ignore ai_best_practices.yaml and to commit AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/. It also lists optional ignore rules for teams that want agent context to stay local.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: ai_best_practices.yaml is now treated as per-developer and git-ignored via /ai_best_practices.yaml in .gitignore when the plugin first creates it.

Technical details

ComposerProjectSynchronizer::ensureDefaultConfig() now calls a new private ensureConfigGitIgnored() after it copies ai_best_practices.yaml.dist into the project root. If creating the file fails, it returns early and does not touch .gitignore. The new public constant CONFIG_GITIGNORE_ENTRY is /ai_best_practices.yaml.

The .gitignore handling is conservative. If any existing non-comment line matches ai_best_practices.yaml, the plugin leaves it alone. This check ignores a leading ! or /, so a ! negation counts as the project's choice. A .gitignore that is a symlink or not a regular file is never written to. If it can't be read or written, the plugin warns and tells the user to add the entry manually. Otherwise it appends a comment line and the entry, adding a newline first when the file doesn't end with one.

Because the entry is only added when the plugin creates the file, a project that already tracks it must run git rm --cached ai_best_practices.yaml once. On composer remove, the config file is still deleted, but the .gitignore line is left in place. The .dist file header and .agents/SETUP.md now point to the new guidance.

Upgrade

If ai_best_practices.yaml is already committed, untrack it once:

git rm --cached ai_best_practices.yaml

If the file already exists, the plugin won't add the ignore rule, so add /ai_best_practices.yaml to .gitignore yourself. For local-only agent context, the README suggests also ignoring:

/AGENTS.md
/CLAUDE.md
/GEMINI.md
/.agents/

item.title: #3586448: Disable agent subscriptions for Languages and gate Specific Entities on availability
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586448 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

In AI Context, agents can no longer subscribe to Languages. A language tag on an item no longer ranks it higher for an agent. Items are still dropped when the request language doesn't match, and they are still included in Relevant and Broad when it does. In Minimal mode, items tagged only with a language are no longer injected unless they use Always include. Existing language subscriptions stay in agent config but are ignored. Sites without Dynamic Entity Reference now list Specific Entities as Unavailable on the scope overview, where it used to be missing. Rebuild caches after updating. No update hook or config change is needed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: No config change; existing agent scope_subscriptions.language values are preserved but ignored.
  • New API: getParticipatingSubscriptions() added to the @internal AiContextScopeResolverInterface; ai_context_ai_context_scope_info_alter() is no longer implemented.

Technical details

Languages now overrides supportsSubscriptions() to FALSE and keeps supportsSituationalMatch() as TRUE, so its capability row is language => [FALSE, FALSE, TRUE]. The request language from AiContextLanguageService::detect() is always known, so matchesRequestContext() is never NULL. A subscription could only re-rank items and never broaden reach, the same reasoning as Roles. Form hiding, the "do not allow subscriptions" note, the scoring skip and save-time preservation of stored values follow from the capability.

Changing the capability alone leaked language-only items into Minimal. prefilterItemIdsByScope() is also used for Global index lookup, so non-subscription scopes can't be stripped inside it. The internal resolver (@internal AiContextScopeResolverInterface) gains getParticipatingSubscriptions(). It drops empty lists and scopes that are disabled, unavailable or supportsSubscriptions(): FALSE. The selector and budget calculator call it before prefilter and subscribed-ID resolution. This also fixes the same leak for stored Roles subscriptions.

Specific Entities was handled differently from Languages: ai_context_ai_context_scope_info_alter() removed its entity_item definition when dynamic_entity_reference was missing. That made its capability unreadable, so calculateScopeScore() carried a hardcoded skip list (global, entity_item, target_entity). Now AiContextScopeEntityItem::isAvailable() reports whether DER is installed, the alter hook implementation is removed, and the skip list is gone. Scoring and getParticipatingSubscriptions() decide purely by capability. A stored entity_item subscription on a non-DER site previously scored at the minimum weight and diluted other dimensions (90/91 instead of 90/90). Because the settings tab is now reachable while the scope is unavailable, validateSettingsForm() no longer queries the missing entity_items field, which otherwise threw a QueryException. The local task deriver is the one getScopePlugins() consumer that doesn't gate on availability, so the tab shows up.

Upgrade

Rebuild caches (drush cr) after deploying so plugin definitions and the agent form pick up the new capability and availability. Stored scope_subscriptions.language values on agents are kept but have no effect.

item.title: #3586388: Align scope scoring, language service, and contextual selection behavior
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586388 · 1 contributor · 28 comments

Summary

Scope ordering, subscription scoring and language handling in AI Context now follow one rule. A scope plugin's weight sets both its position in the UI and its influence on scoring, and higher values come first. Entity Bundle and Site Section scoped items are now excluded when no entity or request is available, instead of staying eligible. Content language is now detected the same way for selection, the language scope, and the list and load-by-id function calls. This includes AJAX calls that carry the language only in the Referer header.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Scope plugin weight now means higher = displayed first and scored more strongly (previously lower = first). The AiContextScope attribute default weight changed from 0 to 1, and AiContextScopeBase::getWeight() falls back to 1.
  • New API: New ai_context.detected_language cache context, used by selection cache metadata.

Technical details

Built-in weights are now Global 100, Use Case 70, Entity Type (shown as Entity Bundle) 60, Site Section 50, Tag 40, Language 30 and Specific Entities (entity_item) 10. Scores use the weight directly through a max(1, weight) clamp in AiContextScopeResolver, replacing abs(weight) + 1. Scoring skips scopes where supportsSubscriptions() is FALSE. For plugin IDs with no plugin instance it also skips global, entity_item and target_entity. AiContextScopeManager sorts by weight descending with plugin ID as the tiebreaker. It no longer lists ai_context provider plugins before other modules, so custom plugins can fall between built-ins.

The new Drupal\ai_context\Service\AiContextLanguageService (ai_context.language_service, marked @internal) provides detect(), translateItem() and translateItems(). It replaces AiContextLanguageDetectorTrait, which is deleted, and the private translateItems() copies in AiContextSelector and LoadAiContextItemById. AiContextSelector, AiContextScopeLanguage, ListAiContextItems and LoadAiContextItemById all use it. The AiContextSelector constructor now takes the language service in place of LanguageManagerInterface. AiContextItemRevisionOverviewForm drops its unused languageManager argument. A new AiContextDetectedLanguageCacheContext returns detect() as its value and itself depends on languages:language_content and url.path. AiContextSelector now uses it in place of languages:language_content.

AiContextScopeEntityType gains matchesCurrentContext(): no item values gives NULL (neutral), no current value gives FALSE, otherwise a match test. AiContextScopeSiteSection returns FALSE instead of NULL when there is no current request. ListAiContextItems seeds the current entity from entity_type and entity_id through AiContextCurrentEntityResolver::setCurrentEntity() before filterByCurrentContext(), and clears it in a finally block.

Upgrade

Custom scope plugins that declared a weight for the old "lower is first" ordering need new values. For example, the built-in plugins changed like this:

// AiContextScopeGlobal
weight: 100,   // was -100
// AiContextScopeUseCase
weight: 70,    // was -10
// AiContextScopeLanguage
weight: 30,    // was 0

Pick a value between the built-in weights (for example 65, between Use Case and Entity Bundle) to place a custom scope. Code that calls ListAiContextItems for bundle-scoped content must pass entity_type and entity_id, because bundle-scoped items are now rejected when no entity can be resolved.

item.title: #3586207: Conditional Subcontext Provider Calls
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586207 · 1 contributor · 40 comments

Summary

Conditional subcontext children used to cost one synchronous AI provider call per selected parent, which could dominate agent latency and provider usage. There are now two new settings on the Context item settings page (/admin/config/ai/context/settings/items). One turns AI decisions for conditional children on or off. The other caps how many parents get an AI decision per context resolution (default 3, range 1 to 20). The toggle defaults to on, so existing behavior is preserved apart from the new cap of 3. If AI decisions are off, all conditional children are included with no provider call. Parents over the cap keep their required children, but their conditional children are dropped. Identical decisions within one request are cached.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: ai_context_update_10010() adds the two new settings to existing sites.
  • Config change: New ai_context.settings keys conditional_subcontext_enabled (default true) and conditional_max_parents (default 3, range 1 to 20); subcontext_enabled checkbox moved to the Context item settings form.

Technical details

AiContextSubcontextResolver::resolve() reads conditional_subcontext_enabled and conditional_max_parents (clamped to 1..20) and passes a by-reference $conditional_calls_made counter through resolveForParent() into resolveConditionalChildren(). The cap is checked before any prompt or provider work. Once reached, the parent's conditional children are dropped and an info message is logged. Which parents are dropped follows internal processing order, not relevance to the task. Calls are one per parent and are not batched.

A per-instance $decisionCache is keyed by md5(parent id | task | sorted candidate ids). It stores approved results, and it also stores empty results from a missing provider, a provider with no chat(), a bad response or an exception, so a broken provider is not re-hit within the request. Cap skips are deliberately not cached. A later resolve() call with budget left can still make the call.

The form layout changed too. The subcontext_enabled checkbox moved from AiContextSettingsForm to AiContextItemSettingsForm, which gains the two new fields with #states visibility. The provider field in AiContextSettingsForm gets a - None - option. Clearing the provider is now blocked only when conditional AI decisions are enabled and published conditional items exist. The provider description now says whether AI decisions are on. Config schema adds the two keys, with a Range constraint of 1 to 20 on conditional_max_parents.

Upgrade

ai_context_update_10010() sets conditional_subcontext_enabled: true and conditional_max_parents: 3 in ai_context.settings when they are unset. Run drush updb. Sites exporting config should export the two new keys.

item.title: #3586416: Clean stale scope values when options are deleted
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586416 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

Context items and agent subscriptions no longer keep scope values for options that have been removed. Deleting a content type, taxonomy term, vocabulary, context tag, language or role now removes that value from items, subscriptions and the scope index. Removing an entity type from Entity Types settings, or a site section from settings, does the same. Uninstalling a module that provided those options also triggers a scrub. Deleting a bundle keeps the type-level type:_all value, but removing the whole type from settings removes it. Use Case values are never scrubbed. After upgrading, run drush updatedb: a one-time post-update cleans up leftovers that already exist. Because updates normally run before config import, on a lower environment with a copied production database this scrub can remove values for options the import is about to add.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: Post-update ai_context_post_update_0006_scrub_stale_scope_values() strips already-stale scope values from items, agent subscriptions and the scope index.
  • New API: New optional AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface for scope plugins whose options can disappear; new AiContextScopeCleanupService methods scrubScope(), scrubStaleScopeValues(), scrubScopesAfterEntityDelete(), scrubScopesAfterBundleDelete(), scrubScopeAfterSettingsChange().

Technical details

The existing ai_context.scope_cleanup service (AiContextScopeCleanupService) still only strips values. The decision about what is stale moved into scope plugins through the new optional AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface: getStaleStoredValues(), shouldScrubAfterEntityDelete(), getStaleStoredValuesForEntityDelete(), shouldScrubAfterBundleDelete() and shouldScrubAfterSettingsChange(). The service now takes plugin.manager.ai_context_scope, collects stored values from the scope index (new AiContextScopeIndexService::getIndexedScopeValues()) and from raw ai_context.agents subscriptions, then asks the plugin which are stale. AiContextScopeInterface is unchanged.

Triggers are generic and do not special-case plugin IDs: ai_context_entity_delete(), the new ai_context_entity_bundle_delete(), and the new ai_context_modules_uninstalled(). The last skips config sync and skips uninstalling ai_context itself. AiContextScopeConfigSubscriber now reacts to any ai_context.scope_settings.{plugin_id} save and skips it while config.installer isSyncing(), because a mid-import scrub would compare stored values to a half-imported environment. Bundle-delete hooks still run during sync.

Plugin policy: Language, Roles, Tag and Entity Types treat a value as stale if it is missing from getAlteredValues(), via the new AiContextScopeBase::getStoredValuesMissingFromAlteredValues(). Site Section also keeps custom: patterns. Taxonomy Terms keeps a value if the term exists and is not in the ai_context_tags vocabulary, or an alter hook added it. Term, language and role deletes return the deleted ID for a cheap strip. A vocabulary delete returns NULL for a full scan. Entity Types scrubs after a bundle delete only when that entity type is enabled in settings, and after any settings save. Use Case, Global and Entity Item do not implement the interface.

Upgrade

Run the new post-update after deploying:

drush updatedb -y
drush cr

ai_context_post_update_0006_scrub_stale_scope_values() runs against the environment as it exists at that moment, before drush config:import in standard pipelines. On a lower environment with a copied production database it can remove values for options that the pending import would add.

Custom scope plugins that can lose options can implement AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface (in the Drupal\ai_context\Plugin\AiContextScope namespace) alongside AiContextScopeInterface. Plugins that do not implement it are left alone.

item.title: #3586471: Fix CCC scope index, stored-value cleanup, and request matching
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586471 · 1 contributor · 48 comments

Summary

Several scope-data bugs in AI Context are fixed. Saving a draft of a published item no longer rewrites the live scope index, so a published Global item stays findable by prefilters while a draft is pending. Unchecking an entity type on the Entity Types settings page is now blocked, with an error naming the usage, while context items or consumer subscriptions still reference it. Language values are no longer deleted on single-language sites. Deleting the last bundle of a type keeps type:_all. Taxonomy matching now uses the revision or translation of the requested entity, and language detection honours a caller-supplied path such as /es/.... The Global checkbox stays visible on the item form when the Global scope is disabled, so existing global items can be cleared. Inheriting subcontexts score using the parent's values when a scope plugin is missing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Service ai_context.language_service now receives @ai_context.request_info_resolver instead of @request_stack.
  • New API: AiContextScopeCleanupService gains public getStoredValuesWithPrefix() and countStoredValueUsage(); AiContextScopeEntityType implements validateSettingsForm().

Technical details

Index: ai_context_ai_context_item_update() in ai_context.module returns early when !$entity->isDefaultRevision(). The cascade to inheriting children now runs only if the original revision was a default revision and its scope differs. Publishing a draft therefore no longer compares against a draft whose scope was never written to the children.

Cleanup: AiContextScopeEntityType::validateSettingsForm() collects stored values for removed types via AiContextScopeCleanupService::getStoredValuesWithPrefix(). It counts usage with countStoredValueUsage(), which skips inheriting subcontexts, and sets a form error. getContentEntityTypeOptions() keeps a configured type listed even with no bundles. getValues() keeps the All option for a bundled type with no bundles, so the generic stale-value diff never reports type:_all missing after the last bundle delete. Live and settings-change scrubs skip disabled or unavailable plugins. Entity and bundle delete scrubs still run regardless. This is documented on AiContextScopeStoredValueInterface: a plugin returning NULL from getStaleStoredValuesForEntityDelete() gets a full getStaleStoredValues() scan even while the scope is disabled.

Matching: AiContextScopeResolver scoring falls back to $item->getScopeItem()->getScopeValues() instead of the child's own empty scope. AiContextLanguageService now takes AiContextRequestInfoResolver (service definition changed) and extracts the language prefix from the single path returned by getPath(). Taxonomy changes are in AiContextScopeTaxonomy and AiContextRequestInfoResolver. The summary describes the intended behaviour; I did not read that diff in full.

Running composer reinstall drupal/ai_best_practices or composer install --no-dev (when the package is a dev requirement) no longer wipes the project's ai_best_practices.yaml or the plugin's entries in composer.json. item.title: #3583075: Rename ContextDefinitionNormalizer now that it normalizes input and output definitions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583075 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Tool module's JSON Schema builder for input and output definitions is renamed from ContextDefinitionNormalizer to InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer. The old name described core's context system, which the definition families no longer build on. The old class name and service ID keep working for one release but trigger deprecation notices. Behavior is unchanged. Custom code that extends the class, uses its constants, or injects it by service ID should switch to the new names before rc1.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The JSON Schema normalizer for input and output definitions is now Drupal\tool\Normalizer\InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer, with the same DECIMAL_PATTERN and DERIVED_ENUM_LIMIT constants.
  • Deprecation: Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer and the tool.normalizer.context_definition service are deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta12 and removed from tool:1.0.0-rc1. Use InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer and tool.normalizer.input_output_definition.

The full implementation moved into src/Normalizer/InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer.php. Its docblock now names the input and output definition families as the subject. Core ContextDefinitionInterface support is described as the ai module's override path. ContextDefinitionNormalizer stays as a thin shell that extends the new class. Its constructor calls @trigger_error() with E_USER_DEPRECATED, and its docblock carries @deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta12 and is removed from tool:1.0.0-rc1.

In tool.services.yml the service is now tool.normalizer.input_output_definition, still tagged normalizer with priority 100. tool.normalizer.context_definition stays as a private alias with a deprecated message. Normalizers are private services, so the old ID resolves only where another service definition injects it by ID. A new kernel test, ContextDefinitionNormalizerDeprecationTest, covers the class and alias deprecations. Internal references were updated: LegacyTypedDataNormalizer uses InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer::DECIMAL_PATTERN, and comments in EntityHandleTransformer and EffectiveDataDefinition plus NormalizerFormatRestrictionTest were changed to match. // After

Behavioral evals can now run against Kiro CLI as well as claude, codex, gemini and mistral. Affects module maintainers.

The provider is run_kiro() in evals/providers.py, registered in PROVIDERS, PROVIDER_DEFAULTS and ISOLATION_MODES. It calls kiro-cli chat --agent-engine v3 --no-interactive --trust-tools= --output-format stream-json --model <model> from a fresh temporary directory. The merged code differs from the issue text: the prompt goes on stdin rather than after --, which also avoids Kiro parsing the skill's --- frontmatter as an option. The output is stream-json, not plain text. The default model is claude-sonnet-5, not auto, because auto picks a model per task and runs would not compare.

Older kiro-cli releases leave their agent server running with the inherited stdout, so stdout and stderr go to temp files, the process is started in its own session, and the whole process group is killed after wait(). Each call gets a throwaway KIRO_HOME, so the operator's ~/.kiro steering, skills and agents do not load. _kiro_context() reads the steering from the session log under KIRO_HOME and the skills and agents from the stream's command list. It raises ContextLeakError for anything that is not bundled with Kiro, or when no session log exists. Per the docs, kiro-cli 2.16 still read ~/.kiro with KIRO_HOME set, so it is unsupported. test_scoring.py tests this against a fake kiro-cli. item.title: #3586791: Add Refusal Answer type to support OpenAI Decision API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)

Summary

The AI module's Decision operation can now represent a model declining to answer an individual question. Previously a refusal, which OpenAI's Decision API can return, was treated as broken output and failed the whole response. Models that declare the new decision_refusals capability may now refuse single questions while the other answers stay usable. Refusals from models that don't declare it still count as broken output.

A new final class Drupal\ai\OperationType\Decision\Value\RefusalAnswer implements AnswerInterface. Its type is 'refusal' (RefusalAnswer::TYPE), getRaw() keeps the provider's wire data, and toArray() returns only ['type' => 'refusal']. AnswerFactory::fromArray() gains a refusal case.

AnswerValidation::forQuestion() takes a third parameter bool $allow_refusal = FALSE. A RefusalAnswer is accepted for any question type when it is TRUE, and otherwise throws \InvalidArgumentException. DecisionValidationEventSubscriber::postGenerate() only resolves the model's capabilities when the answer is a refusal. It checks the provider's getDecisionCapabilities() for AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals. If the provider or model can't be resolved, it counts as not declared, and the InvalidArgumentException becomes AiBrokenOutputException.

On DecisionResponse, isRefused($id) and getRefusals() (question ids) were added. getNoul(), getChoice() and getScore() now throw the new AiDecisionRefusedException (an \UnexpectedValueException implementing AiExceptionInterface) when the question was refused, instead of the type-mismatch error.
